summary:
The world is pretty but it never changes. Every wave of every voyage looks the same: a mid-afternoon sun at the same place in the sky (world.js SUN, line 16), the same blue gradient, the same white cloud floor and puffs, and fixed fog. The regions exist only as a name that flashes up (world.js regionAt). Port and title sit in a dark void with a stone berth (port.js makeVoid). The one exception is the cloud pattern, which slides slowly.

The good news is that almost every colour is a hard-coded constant inside a few small shaders (SKY_GLSL line 31, the deck lines 144-146, the puffs line 202). The ground is a MeshBasicMaterial, whose .color multiplies the painting at no cost. So the whole mood of the sky can be driven by shared uniforms, adding no draw calls and no texture reads.

I proved this by patching the built game at runtime, with nothing in the repo changed. The script is /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/7e489355-d0a0-5ded-9e0b-bc551db36d16/scratchpad/survey/world/proto.js, driven by shoot.mjs. It produced golden hour, a sunset with rays fanning from the sun, a moonlit night with stars, glowing lanterns and town lights below, a storm with rain and a lightning flash, and the ship's shadow on the cloud floor with a rainbow glory round it. The pictures are in the same folder: laptop-golden.png, laptop-sunset-sun.png, laptop-night.png, laptop-night-city.png, laptop-storm.png, laptop-storm-flash.png and laptop-glory.png. I also made the port into a sky dock above a cloud sea (port.mjs, port-laptop-dusk.png and port-laptop-storm.png).

Cost, measured in software rendering at phone size (624x1350, perf2.mjs), each layer drawn alone:
- sky 23 ms, cloud floor 61 ms, ground 90-95 ms, puffs 25 ms. The ship, its shadows and the rest come to about 450 of the 660 ms frame. The cloud noise is already baked in polished (makeCloudBake), so it is no longer the worst cost.
- With every prototype change on, the sky rose to 27-30 ms and the floor to 62-82 ms (noisy). The whole frame went from 660 to 668-697 ms.
- Rain was the only clear cost: 900 streaks added about 10%, so phones should get about 350.

Top recommendation: build one sky module first, src/game/sky.js, that owns the voyage's time of day, the weather and the region's air. A voyage then runs from afternoon through golden hour and sunset to a moonlit night and back to dawn. Night, storms, region moods, the port's looks and the glory all hang on that module. After it, build the moonlit night (the ships' lanterns and sunstone crystals were made for it), storms that roll in for some waves, and clouds you can really fly through.
architecture:
ONE NEW MODULE: src/game/sky.js (the sky director). It owns the look of the world, and the other files read from it. It follows the pattern world.js already uses for `time` and `uCloud`, where shared uniform objects are handed to several materials.

What sky.js exports:
- `SKYU`: the shared uniforms, each a {value} object.
  - Sky colours: uZen, uMid, uHor, uWarm, uSunCol, uBelow.
  - Cloud floor and puffs: uDeckLit, uDeckShade, uDeckUnder, uPuffLit, uPuffShade.
  - Mood: uNight, uRays, uFlash, uGlory, uCoverBias, uStorm, uStormDir, uThin.
  - Ship shadow and mist: uShip, uShipH, uInCloud.
  - uSun stays the existing shared SUN Vector3. It already reaches the sky, the floor and the ground's cloud shadows.
- `KEYS`: keyframes on a day value T from 0 to 1. Each key holds the sun direction, every colour, the sun light and hemi light colours and strengths, fog colour, near and far, ground tint, environment strength, exposure, glow boost and cloud cover bias.
  - T = 0 must equal today's values exactly, so check.mjs pictures and the hangar page stay the same.
- `STORM` (the storm key) and `REGION_AIR` (per-region tints and particle kinds).
- `makeSky({ renderer, scene, world, sun, hemi, envScene, touch })`, which returns:
  - `T` and `weather`
  - `set(T)` and `toward(T, seconds)`
  - `startStorm(dir)`, `clearWeather(seconds)`, `inCloud`
  - `update(dt, { player, camera, time, region })`
  - `bake()`, which re-draws the sky light on the brass

What update() does each frame:
- Blends the current state toward its target: time of day, then storm, then region air, then the height near the Thinning.
- Writes the uniforms, scene.fog, sun.color and intensity, hemi colours and intensity, scene.environmentIntensity, renderer.toneMappingExposure, the ground tiles' and sea's material.color, and the ship glow boost.
- Places the sun light. This moves main.js line 449 into sky.js.
- At the end of a transition, calls bake(). It keeps one PMREMGenerator alive (main.js line 51 makes a new one every time), uses size 128 on phones, and disposes the old texture. The port must keep its own bake so the old texture is never disposed under it.
- On a lost graphics context (main.js line 72), call sky.bake() instead of skyLight().

CHANGES IN world.js:
- SKY_GLSL line 31: replace the constants with the uniforms.
- makeSky lines 44-48: sun colour, below-horizon colour, stars, rays, horizon towers and the lightning flash.
- Deck lines 140-153: colours, cover bias, storm front, ship shadow and glory, flash.
- Puffs line 202: tinting.
- Ground shade() line 119: cover bias, optional sea glitter. Bump the program cache key.
- makeWorld should also return `tiles` and `sea`.
- New makers in world.js:
  - `makeAir(touch)`: one quad-streak mesh for rain, snow, dust and wisps, with a mode uniform.
  - `makeVeil()`: the full-screen mist when inside a cloud.
  - `makeTownLights(spots)`: night lights on the ground.
  - `makeLightning()`: a 16-segment ribbon in a small dynamic buffer.
  - Optional: `makeScud()`, `makeBirds()`, `makeGlare()`.
- makePuffs gains `inside(p)` (a CPU copy of the 110 offsets, wrapped like its vertex shader) and `bank(center)` (6 extra instances placed at run time).
- A JS port of the cloud bake's h2/n2 noise and cover(), so the game can tell when it is in the cloud floor.

CHANGES IN src/ship/build.js:
- Export `GLOW = { value: 1 }` and use it as uniform uGlow in glowPoints (lines 80-91), scaling point size and alpha.
- Raiders' clones share the material, so they follow. The hangar page stays at 1.

CHANGES IN main.js:
- Create the sky after line 58.
- tick() line 447-449: call sky.update after placeCamera.
- sail() line ~110: sky.set(0) and clearWeather.
- waves() line 228 (wave start): sky.toward(dayAt(W.n)), and startStorm if wave.storm.
- Line 241 (wave beaten): clearWeather, plus a plain-words line about the light on the card.
- Expose `__game.sky` for tests.

CHANGES IN progress.js:
- SKIES gains `storms`, the wave numbers that bring a storm on each skies.
- raiders.js waveAt() adds `storm: true` so the "next wave" card can say so.

CHANGES IN port.js:
- makePort receives `world`.
- makeVoid becomes a sky dome with its own copy of SKYU.
- Add a cloud-sea plane that shares world.deck's geometry and a cloned deck material.
- Add motes, plus lantern posts on the berth.
- Add `look` per screen: the title follows the chosen skies, the port shows dusk.

EVENTS:
- Push {type: 'thunder', delay}, {type: 'rain', on} and {type: 'gust'} onto the effects/event bus that the combat-feel survey proposed (fx-core), so the sound work can hook in.
- If that bus is not built yet, a plain array on __game.sky.events will do.

TEST HOOKS:
- __game.sky.{T, set, toward, weather, inCloud, lightningCount, look}
- __game.world.{puffs.inside, puffs.positionOf, air, veil, townLights}
- Every proposal's test reads the canvas with gl.readPixels straight after a renderer.render in the same evaluate call, or reads uniform values. I used this in scratch: toDataURL after render in the same task works; page screenshots of the canvas are unreliable for pixel compares.

EVIDENCE (scratch, read-only, all under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/7e489355-d0a0-5ded-9e0b-bc551db36d16/scratchpad/survey/world/):
- proto.js (runtime patch), shoot.mjs, perf.mjs, perf2.mjs, port.mjs, incloud.mjs (how often a ship is inside a puff), towns.png (the Magpie page's town pixels do NOT line up with this map), grid.png (a gridded minimap for picking town-light spots).

proposals.title: A day passes over a voyage: afternoon, golden hour, sunset, night, dawn
proposals.chris_sees: The voyage starts in the bright afternoon he knows. As he beats waves the sun sinks. By wave 3 the light is gold and the clouds are cream and peach. Wave 5's raider captain is fought against a burning sunset, with rays fanning out of the sun. By wave 7 it is night, the Man-o'-war of wave 12 comes at dawn, and wave 15 is back to afternoon. While the 'Wave beaten' card is up, the sun visibly slides for a few seconds, and the card adds a short line such as 'The sun is going down.'
proposals.why: Today every wave looks identical, so a voyage feels like a loop. A changing sky turns it into a journey, gives the milestone waves (captains, the treasure ship, the Man-o'-war) their own look and screenshot moment, and is the base for night, storms and region moods. It is almost free: colours in shaders.
proposals.how:
New src/game/sky.js, as described under 'architecture'.

Keyframes on a day value T, with each key's sun direction and colours; prototype values are in proto.js MOODS:
- 0: afternoon. Exactly today's constants: world.js lines 31, 46-47, 144-146, 202; HAZE 0xc9d6e6 with fog 4000/34000; sun 0xfff0d6 at 2.6; hemi 0xc3dcff/0x7c8a5c at 0.75; environment 0.9.
- 0.14: golden. Sun direction (-0.69, 0.26, 0.31); horizon (1.0, 0.8, 0.56); warm (1.0, 0.66, 0.36); floor lit (1.0, 0.84, 0.62); ground tint (1.0, 0.84, 0.66); fog 0xf0c49a; sun light 0xffb878 at 2.5; rays 0.6.
- 0.27: sunset. Sun direction (-0.69, 0.07, 0.31); zenith (0.1, 0.14, 0.34); mid (0.55, 0.38, 0.5); horizon (1.0, 0.58, 0.32); ground (0.66, 0.5, 0.48); sun light 0xff9050 at 1.8; rays 1.
- 0.34: dusk.
- 0.42 to 0.70: night (see moonlit-night).
- 0.77: dawn, 0.86: morning, 0.95: noon.

Sun direction moves along an arc: azimuth stays west-south-west and elevation comes from T.

World.js changes:
- SKY_GLSL line 31 becomes `vec3 zen = uZen, mid = uMid, hor = uHor, warm = uWarm;`.
- The sun-disc colour (line 46) becomes uSunCol and the below-horizon colour (line 47) becomes uBelow.
- Add the rays to makeSky: an angle around the sun's axis, `fan = (0.5+0.5*sin(ang*17+sin(ang*5)*2))*(0.5+0.5*sin(ang*7-1.3))`, times `pow(s,5)*(1-smoothstep(-0.05,0.45,d.y))*uRays*0.45` (from proto.js).
- Floor lines 144-145 use uDeckLit, uDeckShade and uDeckUnder.
- Puffs line 202: `mix(uPuffShade, uPuffLit, vUv.y)`.
- The ground is tinted through tile and sea material.color, a MeshBasic colour that multiplies the painting at no cost.

main.js changes:
- Replace lines 447 and 449 with `sky.update(dt, {player, camera, time})`.
- In sail() (around line 110) call `sky.set(0)`.
- At the wave start (line 228) call `sky.toward(dayAt(W.n), 5)`, with `dayAt = n => (n*0.07) % 1`, so the 15 scripted waves make one day. During a fight T creeps forward by 0.0002 a second.
- On 'Wave beaten' (lines 241-246) add the next key's plain line.

Brass reflections: envScene (line 50) already holds a clone of the sky mesh that shares its material, so re-baking it with one kept PMREMGenerator follows the mood. Do it at the end of each transition, behind the card. Give the port its own bake so the old texture can be disposed safely.
proposals.phone_cost: Frame rate: per frame it is uniform writes only; no new draw calls, no new texture reads. The sky gains about 10 ALU per pixel for the rays. Measured in software at phone size (624x1350): sky alone 23 ms before, 27-30 ms after (with stars); cloud floor 61-65 ms before, 62-66 ms after; whole frame 660 ms before, 668-697 ms after, which is within noise. Re-drawing the sky light costs one bake per wave (a few ms on a phone, hidden behind the card). Memory: one environment texture is swapped, not added. File size: a few KB of code.
proposals.test:
In check.mjs:
- fly('brig'), hide #hud, then for T = 0, 0.27 and 0.5: call g.sky.set(T), step 1/60, call renderer.render and read a 16x16 block of sky with gl.readPixels in the same evaluate call.
- Assert the sky's brightness goes day > sunset > night, and that at sunset red > blue.
- Assert renderer.info.render.calls is the same at T 0 and 0.5.
- Assert that after beating wave 1 and sailOn, g.sky's target T is about 0.07.
- At T = 0 the existing shots/ pictures must not change.
- In the whole-voyage block, assert the sky is at T 0 again after a new sail().

proposals.title: A moonlit night: stars, a moon, lanterns, glowing crystals and the towns' lights below
proposals.chris_sees: Night waves fly under a deep blue sky full of twinkling stars, with a big pale moon. The map below turns moonlit blue, with the warm lights of the island city and the villages. Every ship's lanterns, lit windows and sunstone crystals glow brighter, so raiders are spotted by their lanterns far off. The gold shots streak like fireworks, and the Crystal Shards glow like embers.
proposals.why: The ships were built with lanterns, lit windows and glowing crystals (build.js glowPoints, and the partsGlow emissive at 1.6), and these barely show by day. At night they are the star. The prototype shows the Brig's windows and crystals blazing over a moonlit sea, and the city's lights (laptop-night.png, laptop-night-city.png). It also fits Aethermoor: the Magpie page has a 'Moonlight in the Aether' night theme.
proposals.how:
Night keys in sky.js:
- uSun becomes the moon's direction (0.4, 0.5, -0.6). The existing sun disc then draws the moon, the cloud shadows become moon shadows, and the moon's colour is uSunCol (0.8, 0.85, 1.0).
- Sky colours: zenith (0.01, 0.02, 0.06), mid (0.03, 0.05, 0.12), horizon (0.1, 0.13, 0.23).
- Floor: lit (0.13, 0.15, 0.24), shade (0.05, 0.06, 0.11). Puffs: lit (0.2, 0.23, 0.34), shade (0.06, 0.07, 0.12).
- Ground tint (0.07, 0.09, 0.17). Fog 0x0c1020, with far shortened to 20 km.
- Sun light 0x9fb4ff at 0.6. Hemi 0x4a5a90/0x101018 at 0.35. Environment 0.18. Exposure 1.15.

Stars, added to makeSky's fragment: the port's own hash (port.js line 20), `step(0.9965, hash3(floor(d*300)))*smoothstep(0.02,0.4,d.y)*uNight`, twinkling with uTime (pass world.time to the sky).

Glow boost:
- build.js glowPoints (lines 80-91): add a shared `export const GLOW = {value:1}` as uGlow, scaling gl_PointSize by uGlow and alpha by mix(1, 1.3, uGlow-1). Raiders' glows are clones that share the material, so they follow.
- sky.js sets GLOW.value = 1 + 0.8*night.
- Scale art.M.gem.emissiveIntensity (main.js line 451) and art.M.crystal.emissiveIntensity by (1 + 0.6*night).
- Multiply the player's deck lamps (build.js `lamps`) by (1 + night).
- pickups.js gmat point size times (1 + 0.5*night).

Town lights: world.js makeTownLights(). One THREE.Points of about 600 warm points at y = 3, using `gl_PointSize = clamp(26*uScale/-mv.z, 2.5, 11)`, a soft core, a twinkle, and visible only while uNight > 0.05.
- Pick the spots from THIS map. The Magpie page's town pixels are for its angled painting and land about 300 px off (checked in scratch towns.png).
- From the 768x512 minimap: world x = (mx-384)*30, z = (mz-256)*30.
  - The island city at (30, 180), radius 620 m, about 220 points.
  - Villages near (-4980, 60), (-3420, -1530), (-1620, 4230) and (180, 3480).
  - Better still, read the streets and walled districts off the tiles into a small table.

Do not name the moon on screen until Chris says so. The Magpie page's sound list has 'Auros overhead: the Moon's deep, slowly beating hum', so ask him.

Gameplay does not change. The tags still show.
proposals.phone_cost: Frame rate: the town lights are 1 draw call of about 600 points, drawn only at night. Bigger glow points add a little fill. Measured in software at phone size, a whole night frame was 696 ms against 668 ms by day (+4%). The stars add about 6 ALU per sky pixel. Memory: one small buffer of light positions. File size: none.
proposals.test:
In check.mjs:
- Call g.sky.set(0.5), step 1 s, render, and read pixels in the same evaluate call.
- Assert GLOW.value > 1.5 and world.townLights.visible.
- Project player.ship.glow's first point to the screen and assert a warm, bright pixel within 6 px (r > 200 and r > b + 40).
- At T = 0, assert townLights.visible is false and GLOW.value is 1.
- Open dist/hangar.html (if the check opens it) and assert its glow is unchanged (GLOW stays 1, triangle counts the same).

proposals.title: Storms roll in for some waves: a dark front, rain, lightning and gusts
proposals.chris_sees: Before a storm wave, the card says 'A storm is rolling in from the west', and that side of the sky goes dark. When the wave starts, the light dims and the cloud floor thickens and turns slate. Rain streaks slant past the ship, more slanted the faster she flies. Lightning forks down into the clouds a few kilometres off, with a flash that lights up the ship, and the wind gusts. When the wave is beaten, the storm clears and the sun breaks through.
proposals.why: It is the air version of a sea battle in a gale, and it makes waves different from each other. It also makes the three skies, already named after the weather (Fair Winds, Crosswinds, Maelstrom), mean real weather: Fair Winds never storms, and Maelstrom storms often. The prototype is in laptop-storm.png and laptop-storm-flash.png.
proposals.how:
Which waves storm:
- progress.js SKIES gains `storms`: fair has none; cross has waves 8 and 13; mael has waves 4, 8 and 12 (the Man-o'-war in a storm) plus 40% of waves after 15.
- waveAt(n) in raiders.js line 37 returns `storm`, so the next-wave card (main.js line 246) can say so.

sky.js:
- `startStorm(dir)` raises `storm` from 0 to 1 over 20 s and blends toward the storm key. Values from proto.js: zenith (0.16, 0.18, 0.22), horizon (0.42, 0.44, 0.47), floor lit (0.36, 0.38, 0.42), fog 0x4a505a from 1500 to 16000, sun at 0.9, hemi at 0.55, cover bias 0.12.
- Before the storm arrives, the front shows on one side. In the sky and floor shaders: `c = mix(c, stormCol, uStormFront*smoothstep(-0.3, 0.9, dot(normalize(d.xz), uStormDir)))`.

Thicker cloud: CLOUD_GLSL cover() (world.js line 65) becomes `smoothstep(0.44-uCoverBias, 0.64-uCoverBias, ...)`, giving more cloud and darker ground shadows. It needs the floor's uniforms and a uniform in the ground's onBeforeCompile; the prototype does both.

Rain: world.js makeAir(touch). One mesh of N quads, 900 on a laptop and 350 on a phone.
- A seed attribute places each quad in a 120 m box round the camera, scrolled by (rain fall velocity - ship velocity), so the streaks slant with speed.
- Each streak is 5 m long and 6 cm wide.
- Streaks fade out within 8-20 m of the camera (the cost) and beyond 30-60 m.
- Alpha 0.55. Code in proto.js.

Lightning: every 4-12 s, strike 1.5-5 km away.
- A 16-segment jagged ribbon rebuilt on the CPU into a small dynamic buffer: additive, violet-white (0.85, 0.75, 1.0) for the 'Aether storm' the Magpie page's sounds describe, visible for 0.25 s.
- uFlash goes 1, 0.2, 0.8, 0 over 0.35 s, added to the sky, floor and puffs, with hemi intensity multiplied by (1 + 3*flash).
- Push the event {type: 'thunder', delay: distance/343}.

Wind: in a storm, WIND.strength is 0.16-0.24 with gusts of ±30% (flight.js windHelp already uses it, and the raiders feel it too).

After the wave is beaten: clearWeather over 20 s.

Balance: run `node tools/sim-fight.mjs brig 15 mael` before and after, and update docs/game.md 'How hard it is'.
proposals.phone_cost: Frame rate: rain is 1 draw call of thin quads. In software at phone size, 900 streaks (before the near streaks were faded) took the frame from 668 to 740 ms (+10%); 350 faded streaks should cost about 4%. Lightning is 1 tiny draw call for 0.25 s. The storm colours are uniforms only; the front is one dot product per sky and floor pixel. Memory: a few KB of buffers. File size: none.
proposals.test:
In check.mjs:
- Set progress.data.skies = 'mael'. Force wave 4: Object.assign(g.waves, {n: 3, state: 'calm', timer: 0.1, next: null}).
- Step 25 s, then assert g.sky.weather.storm > 0.9, the rain mesh is visible, the cover-bias uniform > 0.1 and wind.strength >= 0.16.
- Step 30 s more and assert g.sky.lightningCount >= 2.
- Clear the raiders by hitting them until the wave is beaten, step 25 s, and assert storm < 0.1.
- Loop waveAt(0..14) on 'fair' and assert there are no storms.
- Assert draw calls during the storm are no more than the baseline plus 2.

proposals.title: Clouds you fly into and through, and raiders bursting out of a cloud bank
proposals.chris_sees: Flying into one of the big clouds, the view fills with soft white mist streaming past. The ship's lanterns glow through it and the world outside fades, then it clears in a breath out the other side. Diving down through the cloud floor, he passes through a layer of mist and comes out under a grey ceiling, with the map sharp below. Small scraps of cloud keep drifting past close by, so he feels the speed. On some waves the raiders' red sails loom out of a cloud bank ahead.
proposals.why: Today a puff just vanishes when the camera gets within 60-260 m of it (world.js line 198), and the cloud floor is a flat sheet, so you never feel inside a cloud. Flying through cloud is the feeling an airship game should have most. It also gives height and speed something to show against, and it sets up a sea-fog tactic. I counted that a ship at flying height is inside a puff at about 6% of places, and crosses one cloud every 2 minutes or so of straight flight (incloud.mjs). So the cloud bank is what makes the moment come up often.
proposals.how:
Knowing when you are in a cloud:
- world.js makePuffs: keep the CPU copies of offs and sizes (lines 182-184). Add `inside(p)`, which wraps each of the 110 positions round uCenter as the vertex shader does (line 193) and returns max(0, 1 - ((dx²+dz²)/(0.7s)² + (dy/(0.38s))²)).
- Port the bake's noise (world.js lines 78-86: h2, n2, 5 octaves) and cover() to JS. Inside the cloud floor (|cam.y - 430| < 45), mist = cover × (1 - |dy|/45).
- sky.inCloud = max of the two, eased.

The veil: one full-screen quad (renderOrder 9, depthTest false, visible only while inCloud > 0.01).
- Its shader reads world.clouds.texture at screen uv × 3, offset by the camera's own velocity, so the mist streams past.
- Alpha = inCloud × (0.55 + 0.45 × pattern), coloured uDeckLit so it follows the time of day.
- Also ease scene.fog toward near 0, far 280 m, in the cloud colour, so ships and ground fade inside.

Scud: a second instanced mesh using cloudTexture(). Forty small wisps, 30-90 m across, in a 1.6 km box round the ship within ±150 m of her height, wrapped like the puffs and faded near the camera.

Cloud bank: makePuffs gets 6 extra instances whose offsets are written at run time (instanceCount 116, `puffs.bank(center)`).
- raiders.spawnWave (lines 142-150) places the bank 500-800 m ahead of the raiders on their line of approach, on every third wave and on storm waves.
- Collapse the bank when the wave ends.

Optional tactic, to be tuned with sim-fight: in raiders.js shoot() line 206, `const e = (dist * r.aim + 1.5) * (1 + 2 * inCloud)` while the Captain is inside a cloud. Document it in docs/game.md.
proposals.phone_cost: Frame rate: the veil is one full-screen pass with 2 texture reads, drawn only while inside a cloud (rare, by the numbers above). The scud is 1 draw call of 40 small transparent quads. The bank adds 6 puffs to the existing draw call. CPU: 110 distance checks a frame (every third frame is enough). Memory and file size: negligible.
proposals.test:
In check.mjs:
- fly; set the player's position to puffs.positionOf(0) (wrapped round the player); step 0.5. Assert g.sky.inCloud > 0.6, veil.visible and scene.fog.far < 600.
- Move 2 km away and 500 m up; step 1. Assert inCloud is 0 and the veil is hidden.
- Put the player at y = 430 over a spot where the JS cover() > 0.7; assert mist > 0.5.
- Check the JS cover() against the GPU: render the cloud floor straight down at 9 points and compare its alpha to the JS cover() within 0.1.
- If the tactic is built: with a frozen Captain, compare raider hits in and out of a cloud over 60 s.

proposals.title: The port becomes a sky dock above the clouds, and the title screen shows the skies you choose
proposals.chris_sees:
In port, the stone berth floats high above a sea of clouds at dusk. There is a warm sky with the first stars, sunstone sparks drift up round the ship, lanterns stand on posts round the berth, and the city's lights glimmer far below. It is still a garage, with the ship turning and the panels as now. On the title screen, picking a sky changes the weather round the ship as he watches:
- Fair Winds: a golden morning.
- Crosswinds: a bright, breezy afternoon with clouds racing past below.
- Maelstrom: a dark storm with rain and lightning flickering on the clouds below.
proposals.why: Port and title are a dark void today (port.js makeVoid). The playtest found the title says 'garage', not 'airships over Aethermoor'. This keeps Chris's racing-garage idea but puts it somewhere in his world, and makes 'choose your skies' something he can see. The prototype is in port-laptop-dusk.png and port-laptop-storm.png.
proposals.how:
port.js:
- makePort receives `world` from main.js line 67.
- makeVoid (lines 15-34) becomes a sky dome running world.js's SKY_GLSL with its own copy of the sky uniforms; keep the void's star hash.
- The cloud sea: `new Mesh(world.deck.geometry, world.deck.material.clone())`, sharing uCloud and uTime with the voyage, at y = -260 under the berth, with renderOrder -5.
- Motes: Points of 160 rising sunstone sparks round the berth. Shader in port.mjs: fract(y + t*0.05) rise, a sine sway, size clamped 1.5-9 px.
- Lantern posts: 6 brass posts on the berth rim (CylinderGeometry plus a small lamp, art.M.brass) with their glows in one Points.

Looks:
- title: follows SKIES[progress.data.skies]. fair is 'dawn', cross is 'afternoon', mael is 'storm', with uFlash flickers every 3-6 s and a small box of the storm's rain mesh.
- port: 'dusk'.
- Each look also sets key.color, rimLight.color and hemi (lines 56-58) so the ship matches the sky.
- The skies buttons (line 106) call setLook when clicked.

The port keeps its own sky-light bake.
proposals.phone_cost: Frame rate: the port gains a cloud plane (4 texture reads per pixel over about half the screen) and a sky dome, about what the voyage's cloud floor costs; nothing is fighting there, and the shadow map stays 1024 on phones. Motes and lanterns add 2 draw calls. Memory and file size: negligible.
proposals.test:
In check.mjs's title section (around line 78):
- Click each skies button. Assert port.look is 'dawn', 'afternoon' or 'storm', and that port.render() raises no errors.
- Assert renderer.info.render.calls in port is 30 or fewer.
- Save shots/title-maelstrom.png and shots/port-dusk.png for Chris's phone.
- The existing buying and upgrade checks are unchanged.

proposals.title: The ship's shadow on the clouds below, with a rainbow ring round it
proposals.chris_sees: Looking down with the sun behind him, he sees his ship's shadow lying on the cloud floor far below. Round it is a small glowing rainbow ring, the 'glory' that pilots see from planes, with a faint white cloud-bow further out. The shadow gets smaller and softer as he climbs.
proposals.why: It is unique, true to flying above clouds, a strong cue for height, and costs a few lines in one shader. The prototype is laptop-glory.png.
proposals.how:
The cloud floor's fragment shader (world.js lines 140-153) gets uniforms uShip (position) and uShipH (height, heading, length).

Shadow:
- Centre: `uShip.xz - uSun.xz/max(uSun.y, 0.08)*(shipY - 430)`.
- An ellipse along the heading, 0.5L by (0.2L + 1% of the height above the floor).
- `col *= 1 - 0.5*shadow*(1 - 0.7*uNight)`, only when seen from above.

Glory:
- `gd = degrees(acos(dot(normalize(vW - cameraPosition), -uSun)))`.
- Rings: red at 6.2°, green at 5.2°, blue at 4.3°, violet at 8.6°, and a warm core within 3°.
- A white cloud-bow at 40°, at 0.07.
- All multiplied by uGlory and by the cloud cover (it only shows on cloud).
- sky.js sets uGlory to 1 with the sun above about 15° and 0 at night or in a storm.
- Wrap it all in `if (uGlory > 0.0)`.

Code ready in proto.js. Optionally, the nearest 4 raiders' shadows via a vec4[4] uniform.
proposals.phone_cost: Frame rate: about 25 ALU per cloud-floor pixel (an acos and a few smoothsteps) and no texture reads. In software at phone size, the floor alone measured 61-66 ms with and without it, which is noise. Memory and file size: none.
proposals.test:
In check.mjs:
- fly; set the cover bias to 0.22 so the floor is overcast.
- Turn the camera away from the sun and pitch it down by the sun's elevation. Render, then read pixels at the projected point opposite the sun and 6° from it.
- With uGlory 1, the ring pixel's R-B difference exceeds that of a plain floor pixel by 10 or more; with uGlory 0 there is no difference.
- Assert uShip follows player.pos after a step.

proposals.title: Each region has its own air: warm hazy Sunscorch Wastes, cold clear Ironspire Peaks
proposals.chris_sees: Over the Sunscorch Wastes the air turns warm and hazy gold, with dust drifting by. Over the Ironspire Peaks the light goes cold and clear blue, with snow flurries. The Gloomfen has low green-grey mist and, at night, pale wandering lights. The Gloamwood is a dusky violet, the Hearthsea clear and bright, and the Open Sea deep blue and windy. The region's name shows as now, with a short line under it such as 'Hot, dusty air'.
proposals.why: The regions are already in the code (world.js NAMES line 21, regionAt) but only as a name that flashes up. Giving each its own air makes Chris's map feel like a world you fly across, without touching the flat painted ground.
proposals.how:
world.js: a REGION_AIR table next to NAMES, giving each region a fog colour, a fog distance scale, sun warmth, a hemi tint, a cover-bias offset and a particle kind:
- Sunscorch Wastes: fog 0xe6c9a0 at 0.6x distance, sun 0xffe2b8, cover -0.05, dust.
- Ironspire Peaks: fog 0xd6e2f4, sun 0xf0f4ff, hemi sky 0xb8d4ff, snow.
- Gloomfen: fog 0xa9b5a2 at 0.55x, cover +0.08, mist by day and wisps at night.
- Gloamwood: fog 0xb4a9c9, light x0.9.
- Hearthsea: fog x1.2, cover -0.06, sea glitter.
- Verdant Wilds: greener hemi ground.
- Open Sea: fog 0xb5c9e6, gulls.

sky.js: read the region every 0.1 s (main.js already does at line 395). Blend its air in over 4 s as a layer of 30% × (1 - 0.5 night) over the time of day.

Particles reuse the storm's makeAir mesh with a mode uniform: dust (warm, slow, sideways, round), snow (white, slow, wobbling), wisps (green-blue, additive, wandering). 200 on phones.

main.js line 396: add a #region-line under #region (demos/game.html line 321, styled like #banner-line), with plain lines for Chris to approve.
proposals.phone_cost: Frame rate: the tints are uniforms only. The particles share the storm's single draw call (200-350 quads) and are drawn only in regions that have them. Memory and file size: negligible.
proposals.test:
In check.mjs:
- fly; player.reset to the middle of a Sunscorch cell (find one by scanning regionAt over the 12x8 grid); step 6 s.
- Assert scene.fog.color.r > scene.fog.color.b + 0.05, the air mode is 'dust', and #region-line holds the Wastes' line.
- Then the Ironspire Peaks: assert fog b > r and the mode is 'snow'.
- Night in the Gloomfen: the mode is 'wisps'.

proposals.title: Towering clouds on the horizon and sun rays fanning from a low sun
proposals.chris_sees: Far off, all round the horizon, big towering clouds stand lit gold on the sun's side, so the sky has depth and the world feels huge. At golden hour and sunset, rays fan out from the sun across the sky. A storm on its way shows as a dark wall of these clouds on one side.
proposals.why: Today the horizon is a plain gradient. A painted skyline of distant clouds gives scale and depth cheaply, and sun rays are the biggest single sunset cue (laptop-sunset-sun.png).
proposals.how:
In makeSky's fragment (world.js lines 44-48):
- Azimuth `u = atan(d.x, d.z)/6.2832 + 0.5`.
- `prof = cloudAt(vec2(u*4.0 + uTime*0.0004, 0.37))`, one read of the existing cloud picture, uCloud.
- Towers where `d.y < 0.03 + 0.09*prof*prof`, with a soft top (smoothstep 0.01), shaded `mix(uHor*0.8, uWarm, max(dot(normalize(d.xz), normalize(uSun.xz)), 0.0))`, and darkened toward the storm colour by uStorm along uStormDir.
- The sky material needs uCloud, so makeSky takes it from makeWorld.

Rays: proto.js's 'fan' lines, with sky.js setting uRays to 1 at sunset, 0.6 at golden hour and 0 otherwise.

The floor's distant haze (line 148) already uses skyColor, so the far edge of the floor blends into them.
proposals.phone_cost: Frame rate: sky pixels only (about 25-35% of the screen), one texture read and about 20 ALU each. In software at phone size, the sky alone went from 23 to 27-30 ms with rays and stars. Memory and file size: none.
proposals.test:
In check.mjs:
- Pitch the camera up (cam.pitch = -0.3) toward the horizon, render, and read a row of pixels just above the horizon.
- With the towers on, brightness varies along the row (standard deviation > 8) where it is smooth today.
- At sunset with the camera aimed at the sun, uRays 1 against 0 changes the pixels at 10° from the sun by more than 15.

proposals.title: Floating rocks at flying height, with glowing crystal veins, to fight around
proposals.chris_sees: Islands of rock hang in the sky at flying height, grass on top, roots and crystal veins underneath that glow at night. He passes them, which shows the speed and the scale. He can duck behind one to break a raider's broadside, and shots that hit them burst into rock dust.
proposals.why: It gives the sky landmarks, depth and cover, which is terrain for sea-battle tactics, while the map stays the simple flat painting Chris asked for. It needs no new art: the rocks are built in code with the ships' own crystal material.
proposals.how:
New src/game/rocks.js.

Shapes: 3 built once. IcosahedronGeometry(1, 3) on a laptop and (1, 2) on a phone.
- Vertices pushed out by the JS port of the cloud noise.
- Top flattened (y > 0.15 becomes 0.15 + small noise); underside stretched into a tapering point (y < 0 becomes y × 2.4).
- Vertex colours: grass and soil on top, banded rock browns and greys on the sides, taken from the map's palette.
- MeshStandardMaterial, vertexColors, roughness 0.95, castShadow false.

Crystal spikes: 3-6 per rock, in one InstancedMesh with art.M.crystal and glow points (GLOW makes them brighter at night).

Placement: about 40 rocks (60-400 m across), seeded between 600 and 1800 m, kept 1.5 km clear of the island city and of the 2.5 km start ring (main.js sail line 95). One InstancedMesh per shape: 3 draw calls, plus 1 for the crystals and 1 for the glows.

Collision, with each rock as a squashed sphere in a 2 km grid:
- guns.js, bolts update: before hitTest, test each bolt segment against nearby rocks. A hit stops the bolt, calls bolts.burst(at, 0xb0a090, 12, 1) and adds a smoke.emit dust puff.
- main.js after player.update: inside a rock, push out along the normal, multiply speed by 0.5, take 2% off the hull, shake the camera and toast 'Scraped the rock'.
- raiders.js steer() 'keep clear' loop (lines 189-194): add rocks as obstacles, keep = radius + 2L + 60.

Later: a picture prompt in docs/art-requests/ for a rock-side texture in the map's style.
proposals.phone_cost: Frame rate: about 40 instances of 320-1280 triangles each (13k-51k triangles) in 3-5 draw calls, lit like the ships but with no shadows. That is under half of one ship (about 100k triangles). CPU: one grid lookup per bolt. Memory: a few hundred KB of geometry. File size: a few KB of code.
proposals.test:
In check.mjs:
- rocks.add(pos, r) 150 m ahead (a hook for tests); fire the bow guns at it. Assert the bolts stop, the hit count doesn't rise, and dust appears.
- A raider set to chase the player through a rock for 60 s never ends up inside a rock's radius.
- Steer the player into a rock; assert she is pushed out and the hull drops by 5% or less.
- In a standard battle, assert renderer.info triangles are no more than today's plus 60k.

proposals.title: Near the Thinning the sky deepens: stars by day and frost at the edges
proposals.chris_sees: Climbing toward 2,400 m, the Thinning, the sky overhead turns deep violet-blue and the brightest stars show even by day. The light gets whiter and harsher, the world below hazes over, and frost creeps into the corners of the screen. Diving back down, it all eases away.
proposals.why: It gives a sense of height, and makes the ceiling a place rather than only the warning message (main.js line 392).
proposals.how:
sky.js computes `thin = smoothstep(1500, 2400, camera.position.y)`:
- Zenith mixes toward (0.03, 0.05, 0.22) and mid toward (0.15, 0.25, 0.55), scaled by thin.
- uNight = max(night, thin*0.5), so the stars show.
- Fog far is multiplied by (1 - 0.3*thin), so the ground hazes over.

Frost: add `<div id="frost">` in demos/game.html with an icy radial-gradient at the edges, opacity thin*0.6, set to display:none when 0.
proposals.phone_cost: Frame rate: uniforms only, plus a CSS overlay shown only above 1,500 m. Memory and file size: none.
proposals.test:
In check.mjs:
- fly; set player.pos.y to 2350; step 1. Assert the zenith uniform's blue > 0.18 and red < 0.06, and #frost opacity > 0.4.
- At y = 700: #frost is hidden and the zenith equals the day key.

proposals.title: Birds that wheel near the ship and scatter at cannon fire (sky creatures only after Chris says)
proposals.chris_sees: Small flocks of birds wheel near the ship: white gulls over the sea and coasts, darker birds over the forests. When the guns fire close by, they scatter.
proposals.why: Life and scale for almost no cost, and scattering birds make the guns feel loud. Aethermoor has sky creatures in its lore: the Magpie page's sounds list an 'Aether serpent' and a 'Sand serpent'. A rare far-off serpent at night would be epic, but Chris should say what they look like first.
proposals.how:
world.js makeBirds() (or birds.js): one InstancedMesh of a 4-triangle bird (a body and two wings).
- 3 flocks of 14 on a laptop, 3 of 8 on a phone.
- The vertex shader flaps the wings from a per-bird phase: wing-tip y += sin(uTime*9 + phase)*0.6*span.
- Each flock's centre circles 200-600 m from the player at her height ±80 m, and members keep a fixed offset plus noise. Better still, compute their positions in the vertex shader from the flock's uniform, so nothing is uploaded each frame.
- When guns fire within 250 m (main.js tick line 435), members fly outward for 3 s.
- Region picks the kind. Hidden at night and in storms.

For creatures, put the question and a picture prompt in docs/art-requests/ before building anything.
proposals.phone_cost: Frame rate: 1 draw call of 170 triangles or fewer. CPU: none if the positions are worked out on the graphics card. Memory and file size: negligible.
proposals.test:
In check.mjs:
- fly; step 2. Assert there are birds and every bird is within 1 km of the player.
- Fire for 0.5 s; assert the mean bird speed more than doubles.
- Set the night key; assert the birds are hidden.

proposals.title: Sunlight glittering on the painted sea, and a moon path at night
proposals.chris_sees: The sea below catches the light: a path of sparkles on the water toward a low sun at golden hour and sunset, and a silver path under the moon at night. The land does not sparkle.
proposals.why: The painted sea is flat colour. Glints make it read as water from high up, and the changing time of day brings the low sun angles where it shines.
proposals.how:
In world.js shade() (ground onBeforeCompile, lines 115-120), after the cloud-shadow line:
- `float water = smoothstep(0.04, 0.16, diffuseColor.b - max(diffuseColor.r, diffuseColor.g*0.85));` (the painted sea is strongly blue and land is not).
- `vec3 v = normalize(vWorld - cameraPosition); float sp = pow(max(dot(reflect(v, vec3(0,1,0)), uSun), 0.0), 120.0);`
- A sparkle cell hash of floor(vWorld.xz/9) + floor(uTime*3).
- `diffuseColor.rgb += uSunCol * water * sp * (0.35 + 1.6*sparkle) * (1.0 - cover)`.

Also on the sea plane (line 132). Bump the cache key to 'ground-cloud-shadow-3'. Put it behind a define so phones can drop it if needed.
proposals.phone_cost: Frame rate: about 20 ALU per ground pixel. The ground is the biggest layer (90-95 ms of about 660 in software at phone size), so expect +5-10% of the ground's cost. It can be compiled out on phones. Memory and file size: none.
proposals.test:
In check.mjs:
- At sunset over the Hearthsea, aim the camera toward the sun.
- Compare a block of sea in line with the sun with the glitter on and off (__game.world.glitter(false)): brighter by more than 10.
- A block of the Sunscorch Wastes does not change.

proposals.title: The sun glares when you look into it
proposals.chris_sees: Turning the camera toward a low sun, a soft glare blooms round it and a few faint coloured rings line up across the screen. It fades when a cloud or the sails pass in front.
proposals.why: Polish that sells bright light and goes with the sunset, at tiny cost.
proposals.how:
world.js makeGlare(): 6 points in one draw (depthTest false, additive, renderOrder 8), placed along the screen line from the sun's projected point through the centre. sky.update works out where they go (SUN projected by the camera).
- Strength = sun on screen × uSunCol × (1 - night).
- Multiplied by (1 - puffs.inside sampled at 3 points along the sun ray, 100-600 m), so clouds block it.
- The big glow is larger when the sun is low. Hidden when the sun is off screen.
proposals.phone_cost: Frame rate: 1 draw call of 6 points, only while the sun is on screen. Memory and file size: none.
proposals.test:
In check.mjs:
- Aim the camera at the sun (cam.yaw to the sun's azimuth minus the heading, pitch to minus its elevation); step. Assert glare.visible and strength > 0.5.
- Look away; assert it is hidden.
- Put a puff centre on the sun ray; assert the strength drops.
